answer: Generally yes. If you were required to file tax returns under nonbankruptcy law, you must file all returns for taxable periods ending in the 4 years before your petition by the day before the first scheduled creditors meeting. For returns not past due at filing, the limit is the later of 120 days after the meeting or the last automatic extension date. The court may extend these periods only if you show circumstances beyond your control.

answer: Under 11 U.S.C. §727(a)(8), the court will not grant a chapter 7 discharge if the debtor received a discharge under §727 (chapter 7), §1141 (chapter 11), or the old Bankruptcy Act in a case commenced within 8 years before the filing date of the new petition. answer: Generally yes, if you are the owner of a copy of the computer program. Archival copies may be leased, sold, or transferred only along with the original copy as part of a transfer of all rights in the program. answer: Under 28 U.S.C. §1407, civil actions pending in different districts that share common questions of fact may be transferred to a single district for coordinated or consolidated pretrial proceedings. The judicial panel on multidistrict litigation makes the transfer, after finding that it will serve the convenience of parties and witnesses and promote the just and efficient conduct of the actions. The panel's transfer order must follow a hearing and be supported by findings of fact and conclusions of law. Each transferred action is remanded to its original district at or before the end of pretrial proceedings, unless it has already been terminated.

answer: The passages describe two routes. First, proceedings in forma pauperis under 28 U.S.C. §1915: a prisoner cannot be barred from bringing a civil action or appeal just because he has no assets to pay the initial partial filing fee, and the court may ask an attorney to represent a person unable to afford counsel. The court must still dismiss the case if the poverty allegation is untrue or the action is frivolous, fails to state a claim, or seeks relief from an immune defendant. Prisoners with 3 or more prior dismissals on those grounds are generally barred unless in imminent danger of serious physical injury. Second, in bankruptcy, a court may waive the chapter 7 filing fee for an individual with income under 150 percent of the poverty line who cannot pay in installments.

answer: Under 28 U.S.C. §1961, interest is allowed on any money judgment in a civil case recovered in a district court. It runs from the date the judgment is entered, at a rate equal to the weekly average 1-year constant maturity Treasury yield for the calendar week preceding the date of the judgment. Interest is computed daily to the date of payment and compounded annually. Different rules apply to internal revenue tax cases, which use the section 6621 underpayment or overpayment rate, and to Court of Federal Claims judgments.
